name: sword-and-shield-run-1
intent: Short, closed-loop backward run cycle with alternating legs in a combat stance: the right hand is the sword hand and the left hand is the shield hand. The backward direction and sword/shield hand assignment are human-approved semantic annotations; preview.gif does not render the props.

phases.name: backward-run-half-cycle-a
phases.description: Half-cycle A of the backward run: motion progresses from knee compression toward stride opening; the pelvis rises and the chest rotates toward extreme A.

phases.name: leg-exchange-a-to-b
phases.description: The legs exchange; the pelvis passes through the high region and then lowers as the leg configuration switches sides.

phases.name: backward-run-half-cycle-b
phases.description: Half-cycle B of the backward run: the opposite knee compresses and then opens into stride; the pelvis rises and the shoulders/torso rotate toward the opposite side.

phases.name: leg-exchange-and-loop-return
phases.description: The legs exchange again, the pelvis lowers, and the motion returns to the looping f0 pose.

keyPoses.description: Peak knee compression of half-cycle A.
Half-cycle A stride opening; the chest reaches its first rotation extreme.
Peak knee compression of half-cycle B; the pelvis is at its lowest point.
Half-cycle B stride opening; both shoulders are near the opposite rotation extreme.

weightTransfer.description: The pelvis shifts laterally along +X from near center at f0 to a maximum around f8, then returns near its initial position by f16. Along +Z it shows two rise-fall pulses: f0→f5→f9 and f9→f12→f16. This is a weight-shift proxy within a backward run cycle.
weightTransfer.contactCaveat: The current evidence is not sufficient to assign the exact weight-bearing leg or contact foot at each frame. The interpretation uses hips/pelvis translation as a proxy rather than directly measured center-of-mass or force data.

bodyMechanics.description: The hips keep rotation around +Z comparatively stable at about −21°, while the chest and both shoulders rotate back and forth more clearly: the first extreme occurs around f2–f3 and the opposite extreme around f11–f12. The arms maintain a combat carriage during the backward run: the right hand is the sword hand and the left hand is the shield hand. The sword/shield hand assignment comes from human review because the prop meshes are not visible in preview.gif.
coordinationFocus: chest and shoulder rotation relative to comparatively stable hips
right-hand sword and left-hand shield combat carriage

recommended: backward run or combat retreat-run motion
right-hand sword and left-hand shield stance
pelvis rise-fall and lateral-shift rhythm during backward running
alternating-leg coordination with an upper-body combat carriage
notRecommended: exact blade or shield-edge trajectory because the props are not rendered in the preview
support-leg or contact-foot identification without additional ground/contact evidence
